scope.completed: Trees consisting of backbone u-v-w with arbitrary pendant leaves at exactly those three possible centers; every bijective destination permutation.
scope.open: Arbitrary trees and caterpillars with unbounded backbone length.
scope.proof_scope_not_closed_applies_to: The unrestricted arbitrary-tree approximation question and longer-backbone generalization only; it does not mean the declared three-center theorem is incomplete.

mathematical_claim.algorithm: Decompose the position-to-destination permutation into cycles. Realize each cycle by q-1 endpoint transpositions; implement each endpoint transposition along the unique tree path by the forward-then-backward edge-swap word, emitting each edge swap in its own round.
mathematical_claim.complexity: O(n) construction time and O(n) output rounds for this diameter-at-most-four class.
mathematical_claim.proof_scope: Three-center caterpillar only; not an arbitrary-tree approximation theorem.

definitions.C_e: Number of token source-to-destination paths crossing edge e.
definitions.r_e: C_e/2; integral by bijective cut balance.
definitions.W_x: Sum of r_e over edges incident to x.
definitions.LB_hub: max(D, max_x W_x), where D is maximum token distance.

verified_steps: For a path of length l, swapping its edges forward and then backward omitting the final edge uses 2l-1 swaps, transposes endpoint tokens, and restores all internal tokens.
For each directed cycle (z1,...,zq), the ordered logical transpositions (z1,z2),...,(z1,zq) sort the cycle; there are q-1 such transpositions.
Tree diameter is at most four, so each logical transposition costs at most seven legal edge swaps.
If m positions are nonfixed, the algorithm uses at most 7m singleton-matching rounds and m <= a+b+c+3.
W(u)=r(uv)+a, W(v)=r(uv)+r(vw)+b, W(w)=r(vw)+c; therefore a+b+c<=3 LB_hub and m<=3 LB_hub+3.
For nonidentity permutations LB_hub>=1, yielding R<=42 LB_hub; identity permutations use zero rounds.
LB_hub is a lower bound on OPT by token distance and per-vertex matching capacity.
An exact five-vertex configuration disproves the direct two-star local preparation condition at cut uv; this is not an impossibility result for all algorithms.

counterexample_to_local_rule.tree: u-v-w with pendant leaf x at u and y at w; no pendant leaf at v
counterexample_to_local_rule.permutation: exchange the tokens at x and y; tokens at u,v,w are fixed
counterexample_to_local_rule.obstruction: For cut uv, an incoming token destined to x is at y, while center v has its own token and no incident pendant leaf holding an outgoing token. The local center-leaf preparation operation is unavailable.

prior_art.citation: Alon, Chung, Graham (1994), Routing Permutations on Graphs via Matchings
prior_art.comparison: Same matching-round model; worst-case routing-number results, not the instance-wise LB_hub bound audited here.

prior_art.citation: Ramras (1993), Routing Permutations on a Graph; Baumslag and Annexstein (1991), A Unified Framework for Off-Line Permutation Routing in Parallel Networks
prior_art.comparison: Equivalent graph-routing and parallel-network terminology checked; no directly equivalent double-star or three-center instance-sensitive bound identified.

prior_art.citation: Kawahara et al. (2019), The Time Complexity of Permutation Routing via Matching, Token Swapping and a Variant
prior_art.comparison: Defines parallel swaps as matchings; path approximation and complexity results, no matching three-center theorem identified.

prior_art.citation: Aichholzer et al. (2022), Hardness of Token Swapping on Trees
prior_art.comparison: Parallel token swapping is NP-hard on general trees; compatible with a fixed-topology subclass result.

prior_art.citation: Bansal, Gunluk, Shapley (2025 revised preprint), Parallel Token Swapping for Qubit Routing
prior_art.comparison: Constant-factor results on cycles, subdivided stars and grids; one-junction subdivided stars do not contain the full three-center class.

prior_art.citation: Sadanandan, Chitturi (2022), Optimal Algorithms for Sorting Permutations with Brooms
prior_art.comparison: Double-broom result optimizes sequential swap count, not matching rounds.

novelty_assessment.note: The checked sources do not state the same instance-wise theorem, but this bounded search cannot establish global novelty; proof ingredients are elementary.
